the JTBD that gym owners are “hiring” member management platforms is changing. The BS that MindBody used to put out about “we’ll help you grow your gym” and “one solution for it all” is total crap and people are falling for it less and less. Gym owners just want something to make life easier. Easier doesn't mean doing my job for me, it means making it easier to do my job: coach, sell, and whatever else I actually enjoy doing in the business

“Your guiding star in understanding your customer's job to be done is their motivation to better their lives. Focusing on functionality will distract you from that" -When Coffee and Kale Compete

Who better understands how gym owners seek to better their lives than someone who did it? This is my argument as to why ClaudeBuilder in OS is the right move

note to future self: when going through the hiring process for OS, two things you're looking for:
1. Someone who is not afraid to take small risks when they see an outsized benefit on the other side of the risk. “ask for forgiveness rather than permission”
2. Someone who cares more about how they did something than what or how much they did of something. The pursuit of personal growth and, secondarily, company growth is the North Star whether they're going through mundane tasks or exciting tasks

Every gym owner says “Oh yeah, I just need something simple for member management, I don't need all the bells and whistles.” Part of that is true, but most of it is not. They don't want something simple with minimal features and scant reporting. They don't want extra clicks to move through your beautiful screens. On the flip side, they don't want 150 different reports, each with 96 filter options. They don't want your 27 email automated sequence with text messaging. They want something that feels natural. It should feel like an extension of their brain that thinks about the business like they do and follows their imagined flow of data. They definitely don't want to trade pretty UI for less detail or information. It should just be organized and placed in the right context so that it's easy to understand what I'm looking at and what my next move is.

Knowing how to get someone to tell you what they really think, as opposed to what they think you want to hear, is proving to be an invaluable skill to hone. Everyone, without realizing it, applies a thin coat of BS to every response to a question that taints their true feelings in an effort to “please” the person asking the question. It doesn't matter if this happens in the workforce, your relationship with your spouse, parenting, that is almost never helpful. If you ask someone a question, you should want to know the complete truth

something to think about for ClaudeBuilder: the gap I've been feeling about the project surrounds the idea of OS becoming the “hub” for gyms to operate out of, creating a true OS. But the problem with the current idea is that it doesn't actually turn it into a hub, it just makes it a really good spoke and semi-aggregator of spokes. The key, I think, to making it the true hub is to bring in the actual data from other platforms/spokes in the businesses tech stack into OS. Thinking the overview page gets a massive overhaul and turns into the OS Dashboard for your business across ALL of its data

the way i think about the “OS Dashboard” idea is that it's the place you come every morning the first time you open your web browser. We would flash the important KPIs that would signal if a closer investigation is necessary. Something like “5 new form submissions overnight” for a CRM platform integration that would present a hot link to take allow you to “zoom in” to that platform where you could look more closely at the data. Once you're done, you “zoom out” and return to OS. The dashboard doesn't need to be exhaustive or complicated. It just needs to show the important metrics that would trip the spidey senses and require closer looks
